messages:
maya: Heads-up — Zenith POC reporting intermittent SSE disconnects only in Safari; stream shows partial JSON objects then parser errors. They're blocked on security questionnaire (SOC2) + Dedicated pricing for trial. Need ops + quote.

devin: do we have their app using native EventSource or a custom fetch stream? Safari differences matter.

maya: native EventSource, confirmed. Chrome works fine for them.

oliver: quick checklist to triage: reproduce with curl, inspect response headers, check for CDN gzip/buffer, and check for rate-limit resets.

sarah: sharing a command for them: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://poc.redwood.ai/stream?trial=zenith" -v` — ask them to capture the raw response and note any long pauses.

maya: customer ran curl: connection stays open but no bytes for ~20s, then client shows incomplete JSON. Browser shows parser throw in console.

devin: that smells like an intermediate buffer or idle timeout. What are our SSE heartbeats?

oliver: default comment heartbeat is 15s (`:hb\n\n`). Some CDNs coalesce small chunks; in Safari that can trigger the parser when multibyte chars split. There was an SDK issue where a split UTF-8 sequence caused parse failure in older Safari builds.

sarah: mitigation options: 1) lower heartbeat to 5-7s, 2) set `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, 3) send a small non-json comment `: \n` every 4s to force flush.

maya: can we flip a canary on the POC route with those headers and heartbeat lowered? Also they hit some 429s during debugging earlier.

oliver: I can deploy a temporary canary: heartbeat=6s, `Cache-Control: no-transform`, `Connection: keep-alive`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Will also whitelist their debug IP 203.0.113.77 for 3 hours to avoid rate-limit artifacts.

devin: infra-bot shows rate_limit events earlier: `infra-bot: rate_limit_event user=zenith_poc ip=203.0.113.77 reason=tokens_exhausted status=429`. That could close connections if token bucket enforcement triggers.

sarah: good catch — whitelist will help confirm whether it's rate-limit induced.

maya: customer also asked for Dedicated pricing and SOC2 attestation text to include in their procurement. Can someone send a short pricing note and confirm compliance posture?

oliver: short note: Dedicated POC typically requires a 1-GPU reserved lane minimum, billed monthly as a commitment; price depends on region — rough ballpark USD 8k–12k/month for single-lane in us-west for POC; exact quote via sales ops. We offer SOC2 Type II and can provide summary and auditor contact. We also support VPC peering, KMS, and configurable log retention (90/365 days).

devin: I'll attach a brief one-pager to legal with those details and loop security for the questionnaire answers.

maya: after we flip canary, customer tried Safari again and still saw truncated JSON at ~18s. curl from their machine behaved the same (stalled then resumed).

sarah: if curl also stalls, that points to edge/proxy buffering or kernel coalescing. Next step: enable packet capture on the edge and collect the raw SSE frames, plus ask the CDN to disable response buffering for that route.

oliver: ordering packet capture now and asking CDN partner to set `proxy_buffering off` for the route. Also enabling `server: no-transform` header.

infra-bot: capture_started id=pcap-1923456789 node=edge-7 region=us-west ts=2026-03-20T09:12:00Z

maya: SDK side — what if customer can't upgrade? Any client workaround?

devin: suggest `event-source-polyfill` for Safari or fall back to websocket proxying. Our SDK supports websocket streaming fallback but requires `enable_ws_fallback=true` on the route.

sarah: send customer step-by-step debug ask: 1) run curl -N and save raw output 2) capture browser console screenshot + network waterfall 3) confirm SDK version 4) try polyfill 5) try again after we enable canary.

maya: customer replied with console screenshot showing `EventSource failed to parse event` and SDK reported `sse_error: utf8_split`. They are on SDK v0.9.0.

devin: that matches the known bug. Recommend upgrading to v0.9.2+. Meanwhile, enable ws fallback on their POC route and keep canary live.

oliver: enabled ws fallback and left heartbeat/caching changes. Infra-bot: `route_patch applied route=poc/zenith canary=true`

infra-bot: route_patch id=rp-778 applied_by=oliver ts=2026-03-20T09:25:42Z

maya: customer tried Safari with ws fallback and reports stream is stable. They asked for a short note to procurement: dedicated POQ pricing and SOC2 language.

sarah: I'll draft an email: "Dedicated POC: 1 GPU-reserved lane, estimated USD 9,500/mo (US-West), includes VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs. SOC2 Type II attestation available; full security questionnaire responses attached." Send to maya for review.

maya: perfect — sending to customer now. Leaving follow-ups: confirm SDK upgrade, after that we can remove ws fallback and revert canary.

devin: leaving a reminder to revert whitelist and canary in 3 hours unless they ask for extension.

maya: thanks everyone — great triage. Will update once procurement responds. :rocket:
